title: Wall tension of a Bose-Einstein condensate: Effects of quantum fluctuations and finite-range interactions
authors: Pham Duy Thanh, Nguyen Van Thu
abstract: We investigate the effects of quantum fluctuations (QFs) and finite-range interatomic interactions on the ground state and wall tension of a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) at zero temperature by means of modified Gross-Pitaevskii equations. The QFs are shown to stiffen the condensate near the hard wall, narrowing the density profile and raising the wall tension above its mean-field value by an amount proportional to square-root of the gas parameter. Finite-range corrections always reduces the wall tension relative to the QFs correction value regardless of the effective range. We find the ordering $γ_0 < γ_{\rm II} < γ_{\rm I}$ in the dilute regime and identify a crossover condition under which the two beyond-mean-field contributions mutually cancel. These results provide an experimentally accessible way for probing beyond-LHY physics through precision measurements of the wall tension in ultracold Bose gases.
summary: This paper theoretically examines how quantum fluctuations and finite interaction ranges affect the wall tension of a Bose-Einstein condensate confined by a hard boundary. By extending the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, the authors predict that QFs increase the tension while finite-range effects partially reduce it. These predictions offer an experimentally accessible method to probe advanced many-body physics in ultracold atomic gases.
main_problem: The study investigates how quantum fluctuations (QFs) and finite-range interatomic interactions modify the ground state properties, specifically the wall tension, of a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC).
main_result: QFs stiffen the BEC near a hard wall, increasing the wall tension above the mean-field prediction. Finite-range corrections partially counteract this enhancement, leading to an experimentally measurable ordering $\gamma_0 < \gamma_{II} < \gamma_I$.
method: The analysis employs successive approximations by modifying the Gross-Pitaevskii equation (GP) using formalisms like CJT for QFs and adding gradient terms for finite-range effects.
model_or_system: The system is a dilute gas of bosonic atoms forming a BEC confined by a hard wall at zero temperature. The theoretical framework evolves from the standard GP equation to modified versions incorporating LHY terms (QFs) and higher-order spatial derivatives (finite range).
key_observables: Wall tension ($\gamma$), density profile ($n(x)$), healing length ($\xi$), and quantum depletion fraction.
important_parameters: Gas parameter ($\alpha_s = na^3/s \ll 1$), effective range ratio ($r_e / 2a_s$), and the LHY correction parameter $\alpha_{1/2s}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on perturbative expansions in the gas parameter and assumes specific functional forms for incorporating QFs and finite-range corrections.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares wave functions from GP vs. MGPI, showing a density notch change; Figure 2 likely compares wave functions across GP, MGPI, and MGPII solutions.
paper_structure: The paper builds theoretically by first establishing the mean-field (GP) baseline, then incorporating QFs via the Modified GP Equation (MGPI), and finally refining this model with finite-range corrections leading to MGPII. The results are presented through quantitative comparisons of derived wall tension formulas.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical roadmap for interpreting high-precision measurements of BEC interfaces, linking measurable quantities like wall tension directly to fundamental many-body physics beyond the standard mean-field theory (LHY and finite range).
